answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a lotus as the anchor of the cost.
